audit_findings.title: Acquisition-driven growth may be valued without its recurring acquisition cost
audit_findings.magnitude: $778.8 million aggregate acquisition consideration in 2024-2025, plus $69.9 million for DCI in 2026; computed total $848.7 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Historical acquired growth enters the growth assumption and OE base, while acquisition cash outlays are excluded from OE as investing cash flows.
audit_findings.evidence: The aggregate consideration, inclusive of contingent consideration and net of cash acquired, for all acquisitions completed in 2025 and 2024 was approximately $631.6 million and $147.2 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The mismatch is demonstrated: acquisitions contributed 3.1% of 2025 revenue growth and 5.0% of first-half 2026 revenue growth, while substantial acquisition spending was omitted from distributable OE. The $778.8 million spent in 2024-2025 exceeds the $654.0 million annual OE anchor. Whether acquisitions are required to sustain the 6% base growth remains unresolved, but a recurring acquisition allowance could materially reduce forecast OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.action: Decompose revenue and OE growth into organic and acquired components, estimate the normalized acquisition spending required for each forecast growth rate, and rerun every scenario either with that spending deducted or with acquisition-dependent growth removed.

audit_findings.title: The unparsed latest-quarter liabilities could conceal claims ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $30.3 million identified earnout fair value; other potentially omitted claims unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquisition and other non-operating liabilities would require separate deductions in the equity bridge if their settlement is not captured in forecast OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company estimates the fair value of this earnout contingent consideration to be approximately $30.3 million, which becomes payable at certain dates through 2028 if certain conditions are achieved.
audit_findings.explanation: The identified earnout is a demonstrated claim, but at approximately $0.35 per diluted share and 0.27% of base equity value it is not material by itself. The broader concern is unresolved because the latest balance sheet aggregates $498.4 million of current accrued liabilities and $434.0 million of other noncurrent liabilities without the supplied record reconciling all components. The record therefore cannot establish the size or materiality of additional omitted claims.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 2026 liability detail and acquisition-accounting schedules; reconcile earnouts, acquisition obligations, deferred compensation, tax contingencies and other non-operating claims, then rerun the bridge for amounts not represented in forecast OE.

audit_findings.title: The forecast may preserve an unusually favorable tax burden
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.2 million of filed 2025 Pillar II tax expense; sustainable additional burden unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An understated sustainable tax rate overstates after-tax OE in every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: We are continuing to evaluate the potential impact of this interpretative guidance and the release of GMT-implementation legislation in other countries, and such guidance or legislation could result in a material increase in our effective tax rate.
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation contains no explicit tax normalization despite a 2025 effective rate of 16.2%, a first-half 2026 effective rate of 19.2%, and the filing's warning of a potentially material GMT increase. These facts demonstrate tax-rate variability, but they do not establish the sustainable rate or isolate how much of the increase should apply to normalized OE. Because the effect compounds through a terminal value representing 51.5% of base operating PV, a persistent increase could be material.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile cash and book taxes by jurisdiction, identify discrete benefits and charges, incorporate enacted GMT rules, calculate a sustainable tax rate, and rerun the OE series and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The entire cash balance may not be excess or freely distributable
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum direct bridge exposure of $320.6 million, or $3.71 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Restricted, operational or tax-leaky cash would reduce the cash addition in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: For many reasons, including the number of legal entities and jurisdictions involved, the complexity of the Company's legal entity structure, the complexity of tax laws in the relevant jurisdictions and the impact of projections of income for future years to any calculations, the Company believes it is not practicable to estimate, within any reasonable range, the amount of additional taxes which may be payable upon the distribution of earnings.
audit_findings.explanation: The distributable portion is unresolved, but even treating none of the $320.6 million as excess would reduce base value from $129.13 to approximately $125.42 per share, only 2.9% of base equity value. It would also reduce bull value to approximately $139.95, still below the $157.12 market price, so the maximum direct bridge correction would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Map cash by entity and jurisdiction, determine minimum operating and restricted cash, estimate repatriation leakage, and replace the bridge addition with demonstrably distributable cash at the next rerun.

audit_findings.title: Existing uncertain-tax claims are absent from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $66.8 million at December 31, 2025, comprising $54.8 million of unrecognized tax benefits and $12.0 million of related interest and penalties
audit_findings.mechanism: Any settlement not already captured in forecast OE would require a deduction from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, we have total unrecognized tax benefits for uncertain tax positions of $54.8 million and $12.0 million of related accrued interest and penalties, net of tax, although we are unable to reasonably estimate the timing over which these liabilities might be paid.
audit_findings.explanation: A full $66.8 million deduction would reduce value by approximately $0.77 per diluted share, or 0.6% of the $11,162 million base equity value. That maximum treatment would not change the conclusion relative to the $129.13 base value, $143.66 bull value, $90.39 buy-below threshold or $157.12 market price.
audit_findings.action: Update the uncertain-tax balances through June 2026, estimate probable settlements and offsets, verify whether expected payments are already represented in OE, and include any net bridge deduction in the next rerun.
